title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Improving Access To Health Services For Disadvantaged Groups Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative:
Tranche 1 proposed for financing under the requested periodic financing request (PFR) aims to contribute to the investment program's impact of improving the health status of Mongolians.
The investment project comprises the following outputs:
(i) urban and rural primary health care strengthened, (ii) district and aimag hospital services improved, (iii) health financing system strengthened, and (iv) capacity in procurement and financial management of relevant government entities for health strengthened.

description.narrative: Access to affordable quality primary and secondary health servicesb in Khovd and Uvs aimags (provinces), Ulaanbaatar ger (traditional tent) areas, and selected soums (aimag subdistricts) improved

45,500 persons per year from Ulaanbaatar ger areas, and selected aimags use gender sensitive and client-friendly expanded PHC services Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 8304 beneficiaries in 2 SHCs (women- 48%, reproductive age women- 15%, elderly people- 13% and disabled-4%). Additionally, served to 1000 migrant- people from neighboring soums. Data Source: MOH and UCHD annual statistics and reports

97,500 persons per year use improved quality district hospital and aimag general services, including modern obstetrics and gynecology, and surgery departments Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 10,503 beneficiaries per year in Uvs AGH (women- 62%; aged over 60 year- 17%). Data Source: MOH and UCHD annual statistics and reports

An integrated strategic purchasing system is initiated involving MOF, HIO, MOH and local governments based on issued regulations Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed. The strategic purchasing system has been established in 2021. Data Source: Ministerial orders, MOH and MOF Base year: 2019
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: A management system for autonomous hospitals is developed, agreed, and operational in at least three hospitals (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: CS04 consultants conducted a situational analysis of hospital governance and management systems, operational and financial performances, risks, and challenges in the provision of quality healthcare services in project hospitals; and study comparing the management capacities of referral hospitals with and without functioning boards in 2023 and 2024. The hospital boards have been strengthened in Uvs AGH and KHUDH, and a new board has been established at Khovd RDTC. The management system for these 3 semiautonomous hospitals are now operational. The recommendations on hospital governance and management systems discussed by various stakeholders; and reviewed at the MOH Management Board in 2024; and the MOH's State Administration Department established a working group has tasked with amending health legislation to regulate hospital management boards. The consultant designed recommendations for improving semi-autonomous hospital management system, submitted to MOH for amendments on Health Law, Law on Medical Care and Services, Law on Health Insurance, Law on Procurement of Goods and Local Property Funds, and MOH's orders (A/476 in 2017, A/254 in A/565 and A/566 in 2019, A/536 in 2019, No.116 in 2019, and No.439 in 2006). During 2023-2025, 154 hospital management staff (87.7% women) from 4 project hospitals participated in training on hospital semi-autonomy and governance. The MOH formally accepted all technical reports submitted by CS04 in July 2025, as included: Technical Report 5: Management Functions for Hospital Autonomy, Governance, Finance, and Management, along with Implementation Tools in Project Hospitals; Technical Report 6: Assessment survey of Hospital Autonomous Operations and Management; Technical Report 7: Financial Management Systems in Project Hospitals; Technical Report 8: Quality and Patient Safety in Project Hospitals. The Completion Report is currently in development. Data Source: MOH and project review reports

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: Five gender and client-friendly SHCs established in selected aimags (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The project will establish four SHCs. One out of the planned five SHCs in Tranche 1 is dropped from the project because the government started its construction using its budget. The CS01 developed functional plans for four SHCs.
The functional plans A, B, and C levels of 5 SHCs were accepted by the MOH TWG in May 2022; the concept designs of the SHCs were approved in Dec 2022. The detailed engineering drawings (DEDs) for 4 SHCs were completed and approved by State Expertise, and the bids were advertised in April- July 2023. The BEC for civil works was established by MOH (order A/68, May 16, 2023). Package CW03 (SHC in Bayan-Under of Uverkangai) was awarded, and CW started in September 2023. Package CW02 (SHC in Erdene of Dornogobi), CW04 (SHC in Tarialan of Khuvsgul), and CW05 (SHC in Dashinchilen of Bulgan) were awarded in September- October 2023. Civil works started in April - May 2024. The construction works for the SHCs in Bayan-Ondur, Uvurkhangai aimag (CW03), and Dashinchilen, Bulgan aimag (CW05), were completed and approved by the State Commission in December 2024 and October 2025, respectively. The progress of CWs for the SHCs (CW02 and CW04) is estimated at 90%-94% completion.
Each SHC has been equipped with 64 types of furniture and medical equipment. Contract progress is 80%, with equipment and furniture installed at the SHCs in Bayan-Under of Uvurkhangai aimag and Dashinchilen in Bulgan aimag. Data Source: MOH yearly project progress reports

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: Four gender and client-friendly FHCs with expanded services set up and providing health services to target population in Ulaanbaatar (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The UCMO fully resolved land issues for constructing 4 FHCs in 14th khoroo Khan-Uul (KHUD), 19th khoroo Chingeltei (CHD), 17th khoroo Bayanzurkh (BZD), and 26th khoroo Songinokhairkhan (SHD) districts.
Functional plans and layouts for gender- and client-friendly 4 FHCs in UB developed Monconsult LLC (CS01) was approved by the MOH in 2022; The FHC in the 14th khoroo of KHUD had already been constructed in 2021-2022 using state budget funds prior to the project's start; therefore, only the LCT heating system will be built for this center under the project. Under the project, the concept design of 3 FHCs developed by Khatanbaatar LLC (CS03) and approved by the UCMO in 2023; and detailed engineering drawings (DEDs) for FHCs approved by State expertise in 2024 and 2025, respectively. The MOH established BEC for civil works (order A/68, May 16, 2023); and were awarded the contracts for FHCs at BZD 17th (CW01) and CHD 19th (CW11) khoroos in 2024, and at SHK 26th khoroo (CW12) in February 2025. Progress of civil works is estimated in BZD 17th khoroo at 50%, CHD 19th khoroo at 77% and SKH 26th khoroo at 93% of the entire work, respectively.
The SKHD Government completed the installation of external sewage pipeline and external electrical work in December 2025. External civil works for infrastructure to new FHCs have not yet commenced due to the ongoing bidding process; however, the Local Government at BZD and CHD is considering the matter, and completion is planned for 2026.
The MOH approved the A/129 order for medical equipment and technical specifications covering 80 items, including gynecology examination couches for 3 FHCs, in March 2024, and awarded Contract G01 to Interscience LLC in September 2024. All equipment was delivered to Mongolia and commissioned by the MOH Technical Committee. Installation, commissioning, and maintenance training have been delayed due to the phased construction of the 3 FHCs. Contract implementation is 80% complete. Data Source: MOH yearly project progress reports

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: Feasibility of LCT in one hospital and three FHCs demonstrated, verified and reported (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing. MOH engaged a consultant firm (CS10) in Dec 2021 to introduce and install advanced LCT, mainly, to monitor and confirm the installation of LCT, which will later be validated by external experts and reported to JFJCM. The CS10 consultant provided comments on the LCT of the DED for KHUD hospital and specifications of the evaluation score for the LCT part of the BD for package CW08 in Section 6; and assisted the BEC in BE. The contract, awarded in December 2023, includes LCT such as high- insulation windows, solar PV panels, an air handling unit (AHU) with efficient heat recovery and fan, and heating, ventilation and air conditioning system (HVAC) with efficient chillers. The contractor submitted LCT equipment specifications 3 times to the CS10 consultants. Of the 4 equipment types reviewed- solar panels, HVAC, AHU, and windows-only the HVAC system fully met the criteria, while the AHU's EC motor fan partially complied. In March 2025, the contractor submitted additional documentation for the remaining LCT equipment for further review. Data Source: Monitoring and verification reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: Khan Uul district hospital of Ulaanbaatar expanded to include surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, and other disciplines; and in- and outpatient departments functionally linked (2019 baseline: NA) Achievement: N Progress/Status: In March 2022, the MOH engaged consulting firm BT LLC (CS18), developed the DED for KHUDH, which was approved by State experts in Dec 2022. Contract for "CW08- KHUDH Construction with equipment installation, including Advanced LCT (windows, solar panels, and HVAC)" was signed between MOH and China Railway First Group Co., Ltd on 20 Dec 2023. MOH engaged the UCMO Investment Department (CS19) as the Employer's supervisor (or Engineer) in June 2023. The construction officially began on-site on 18 May 2024. Contract performance is estimated at 35.6% (CWs 40%, LCT 1% & medical equipment- 1%). Total of 314 staff participated in comprehensive capacity building program across all targeted areas. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: Uvs aimag hospital expanded with a new outpatient department (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Functional flow plan for the extension of Uvs AGH was approved in June 2022, and concept design for the extension was developed in Nov 2022; and DED was developed and approved by the CDC in May 2023. MOH signed a contract for the construction of Uvs AGH extension (CW10) with JV City Landmark LLC and Happy Building LLC in Oct 2023. The work started in May 2024, and Construction of extension was completed in Oct 2025 and officially accepted by the State Commission in Nov 2025 (No.37/2025 dated 31 Dec 2025). MOH (А/38) approved list and technical specification of essential medical and non-medical equipment for the Uvs AGH on 06 Feb 2025 and contracted package G24 with 3 lots: to supply medical equipment on 9 July 2025. Across the 3 lots, the MOH's Technical Committee commissioned all equipment; approved distribution to end users by Health Minister's Order A/374 dated 10 Oct 2025. The equipment was installed and handed over to the end users in Dec 2025 and is now fully operational. Total of 548 participations attended in capacity- building training conducted by the CS04 team. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Health financing system strengthened Indicator: 20% of HIO staff report improved purchasing capacity, including planning and negotiations skills, contracting and contract management, costing, monitoring and reporting, service quality auditing and fund management (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The project trained 18 master trainers in 2021. Mater trainers trained 68% of MOH staff in Module 1: Strategic Purchasing System in December 2021 and Module 2: Hospital Autonomy & Gender-sensitive Budgeting in April 2022. The project conducted 7 capacity-building training for the HIGO staff in March 2022 with the participation of 163 staff (80.9% of them were female) on new legal reforms on single buyer purchasing, strategic financing, selection of healthcare organizations, contracting, service quality, claim control, claim criteria, health services packages, reimbursement method of DRGs, calculation budget, medical auditing, requirements, selection and contracting of medical auditor, and quality assessment on medical services. The project also trained staff from 20 aimags' and remote districts' health insurance departments in modules 1 and module 2 and on the updated HIGO resolutions #1 and #5, regulation on out-pocket payments, procedures on the selection and contracting of the healthcare organization, and performance indicators for the contract. 2300 people participated in the above training (77.8% were women). In January 2024, the MOH engaged five individual consultants for health finance, costing, healthcare package, and healthcare quality. The consultants developed two technical reports: “International Experience in Introducing Health Technology Assessment and Steps to Implement It in Mongolia” and “Assessment Report on the Current Situation of the Health Benefits Package.” The project also trained total of 4,118 medical staff (76.7% women) on health financing reform, strategic purchasing, and strengthening the semi-autonomy of hospitals in 2021- 2022. These participants were from FHCs, SHCs, RDTCs, AGHs, rural general hospital, central and specialized hospitals, university hospital, district health centers and hospitals, maternity hospitals in UB city. On 6 June 2025, the MOH organized a discussion on health sector financing and hospital financial management. During the session, the Health system and Costing and payment mechanism consultants delivered two presentations titled “International trends in health financing” and ”Assessment of the budget and financial status of state-owned health organizations”, respectively. Data Source: Surveys administered to training participants Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Health financing system strengthened Indicator: A strategic purchasing system is designed, and the accompanying road map and regulations issued (2019 baseline: NA) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The Strategic purchasing model in healthcare financing was approved by the Government of Mongolia in 2020 and implementation started in 2021. The project team in collaboration with consultants engaged under TA 9701-MON: Improving Health Sector Financing for Universal Health Coverage conducted a number of capacity-building activities for the Health Insurance General Office (HIGO), MOH, and public hospitals. Under the project, the project consultants developed several official documents and reports, which were subsequently adopted by the National Council on Health Insurance (NCHI) and the MOH. Data Source: Ministerial orders, MOH and MOF reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Health financing system strengthened Indicator: Sex-disaggregated data collection system established for health financing model (2019 baseline: NA). Achievement: N Progress/Status: The government has established a sex-disaggregated health insurance data collection system since 2020. Data Source: Reports and Health Insurance Organization (HIO) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Procurement and financial management capacity of government health entities strengthened Indicator: 60% of relevant MOH and GPA staff trained on procurement, financial and risk management) for health Progress/Status: 85% (92 out of 108) of relevant staff and BEC members of MOH, SPA/GPA, Investment Department of UCMO, and (69.6% women), including the top managers were trained on ADB-financed Procurement policy and guidelines; Procurement of Works and Goods, Consultant Service Recruitment and Open competitive bidding and bid evaluation in 2022-2023. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: 60

Output: Procurement and financial management capacity of government health entities strengthened Indicator: A competency-based capacity building program developed Progress/Status: The MOH engaged procurement consultants CS23:International and CS24: National in 2022. The national consultant developed capacity-building program and training materials for relevant staff of the MOH and GPA based on training needs assessments in Oct 2022 and approved by MOH in Nov 2022. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: An integrated primary and secondary care model piloted (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: MOH engaged a consulting firm (CS01) for PHC development in Dec 2021. CS01 consultants reviewed international experience and proposed a “Hub and spoke” (GER) model for horizontal functional and vertical integration of clinical services in managing 4 types of diseases (hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and tuberculosis) between FHCs and district health centers discussed at four MOH Technical Working Group (TWG) meetings held in 2022 and 2023. Feasibility study was conducted in 2 districts demonstrated that out of all identified integration forms, only few could be implemented within the existing legal environment. The feasibility study of integrated delivery of services in Ulaanbaatar” is submitted to MoH. Four integration forms. i.e., Clinical intregration (common diseases such as hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia and tuberculosis), service integration, functional and information integrations were piloted in Chingeltei and Khan-uul districts from October 2023 to December 2024. Key measures taken to enable the implementation of integration model: a) District Coordinating Committee established in the 2 districts and supervised its implementation, b) resource sharing by consolidated service approved by the Head of UBHD order A/219 on 15 December 2023, c) Job description for social workers amended to be responsible for the referral process d) Job description amended for the head of tuberculosis dispancery that enables better coordination of primary and secondary cooperation, e) clinical capacity-building training (as part of the quality reform initiatives outlined and technical trainings for referral activities were conducted. Evaluation of Intergraded model implementation was completed in February 2025. The technical Report 7 “Model of integrated delivery of service including referral criteria” was submitted to MOH. Based on the integrated care model piloting results, the consultants further elaborated an organizational integration "extended" model that clusters 3-4 FHCs to form a so- called "Community health centers" (CHCs) to maximize PHC services and consolidate services such as laboratory testing, ultrasound diagnostics, and early screenings. The Law of Mongolia on the Legal Status of Towns and Villages will regulate the implementation of UB city structural reform starting 01 January 2026. The concept was discussed among various stakeholders such as MOH, UCMO, UBHD, Society of Family doctors, Mongolian National University of Health Sciences. MOH established a working group in August 2025 that convened twice to discuss the implementation of new integrated care model. MOH's Working group concluded to coordinate structural and organizational changes proposed by CS01 consultants with UBCMO "20 minute city" initiative planning and Government initiated process re-engineering planning of public services. Technical Report-5 “Proposal for organizational and structural integration reform in health sector” was the main document for the MOH TWG to further emerge organizational reform of PHC. Data Source: MOH yearly project progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: LCT installed in one FHC (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: MOH engaged a consulting firm for package CS10: Low Carbon Technology under the JFJCM grant in Dec 2021. The geological survey conducted on each FHC site. BDs for package CW01a for design construction and installation of ground source heating pumps (GSHP) at 3 FHCs were developed; the bid was advertised in Q2 however due to cost escalation, the MOH BEC cancelled and concluded to re-bid. The package was changed into 3 separate packages: CW13, CW14 and CW15 that were re -advertised twice in 2024 and all of them failed. Last BER was cancelled in June 2025 due to received bids exceeded than estimated cost amount of the package. Based on that, BEC of MOH has cancelled package CW13: Design and Build of GSHP for FHC- SKH 26th, and sent revised number of packages with increasing budget for CW14 and CW15 to ADB, which was reviewed and accepted by JFJCM. Re-establishment of bid evaluation committee is pending at MOH. The rebidding willbe advertised in Q1 2026. Data Source: Monitoring and verification reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: National emergency care system established in Ulaanbaatar and aimags (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The MOH engaged a consulting firm CS02: Establishment of emergency medical services (EMS) on 16 June 2023. Consulting firm Vamed Management and Service GmbH submitted inception and 5 technical reports out of 10 reports stated in the contract, have been accepted by MoH. Consultants CS02 developed the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) concept in 2024, which demonstrates structure of national system emergency medical network, where NECC plays a central role in call receiving, triaging, dispatching, and coordinating all emergency calls nationwide. Ministerial Board approved pre- hospital care concept and Training roll out plan for emergency medical care on 22 September 2025. MoH's Department of Policy Planning passed it to Parliament for approval in November 2025 and MoH's Department of State Administration Management will lead the planning and transition to NECC. In addition, MoH initiated negotiation with Ministry of Justice regarding all medical calls received at NECC in August 2025. Training of master trainers organized by the MOH with the project on 22-26 September 2025, and 15 trainers obtained skills for better coaching, training facilitating and communication. The MOH subsequently approved the UK ambulance protocol as the most suitable option for translation and future adaptation. Technical report 8, “Revision and update of emergency care protocols and SOPs” was submitted and accepted by the MOH; and the consultants drafted a Mongolian version of the WHO Basic Emergency Care handbook (MBEC). The functional plan for NECC was developed by CS02 consultants and approved by the MOH Technical Working Group in December 2023; the concept design was executed by the design and supervision consultant Khatanbaatar LLC (CS03) and approved by UCMO's City Planning Agency in June 2024; the concept design amendment was approved by General architect of UCMO on 02 October 2024. The DED of the NECC was approved by the State expertise in January 2025. The BEC in SPA re-advertised of package CW07 in October 2025. The evaluation is completed and a notification on contract award was sent to winning contractor on 24 December 2025. The contract will be signed within Jan 2026. - The list of medical equipment and specifications of advanced- emergency ambulances are finalized and will be presented in the MOH technical working group. Equipment list and technical specification, and room to room book for NECC have been prepared. The MOH's Technical Working Group discussion at MOH is pending. Timely coordination is crucial to synchronize the supply and installation of goods and equipment with the construction schedule. Due to the re-advertisement of CW07: construction of NECC, the IFB and expected CAs would be postponed to Q1 2026.
Data Source: National emergency care center yearly reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N
